review_asks.title: No internal owner is recorded for either external dependency (GitHub report link, ACE OLEDB redistributable) — who should be asked whether they survive modernization?
review_asks.why: Without a named internal owner, nobody can be asked whether these two external touchpoints should be carried into any target state or retired.

confidence.rationale: Both dependencies are directly evidenced in source (a hardcoded GitHub URL launched via Process.Start, and the ACE OLEDB 12.0 provider reference), and neither the catalog nor the structural-analysis pass records an internal owner for either.

review_asks.assessment: Two external dependencies were found: a hardcoded public GitHub link (the dashboard's 'Report' button shells out to a PDF via Process.Start) and the Microsoft ACE OLEDB 12.0 runtime redistributable required on every workstation to reach the Access database. Neither has a recorded internal owner.
review_asks.reasoning: A scan of catalog.json, structural-analysis.json's integration_points/interface-inventory sections, and call-graph.json surfaced exactly these two outbound touchpoints — there are zero HTTP endpoints, zero message queues, and zero scheduled jobs otherwise. Discovery recorded both with technical detail but no owner field.

review_asks.title: Confirm the integration graph is complete for this single-application wave
review_asks.why: Downstream Rationalization and sequencing steps will treat this graph as the whole integration picture for the wave; an undiscovered integration would surface later as a failed cutover rather than a flagged risk.

confidence.rationale: Discovery's structural-analysis pass read every one of the 13 .vb files, the .vbproj, the .sln and all config/manifest files in full (an explicit do-not-fan-out case: 1 build module, 2,787 LOC, 1 table) and found zero HTTP endpoints, zero scheduled jobs, zero message queues, zero stored procedures/views/triggers/links, and exactly one local file-based database. The only outbound call is a hardcoded browser launch.

review_asks.assessment: This wave contains exactly one application: a standalone VB.NET WinForms desktop app with no network, web, batch, or API surface, persisting to a local Microsoft Access file. There are no cross-app integrations to record because there is no peer application in this wave.
review_asks.reasoning: systems[] holds the one in-scope application; data_flows[], shared_identifiers[], and cross_system_capabilities[] are empty by construction (a cross-app artifact needs ≥2 systems to populate them), and both discovered external touchpoints are captured in external_deps[]. Nothing in the Discovery evidence (catalog, structural-analysis, call-graph) suggests an undiscovered integration.

review_asks.title: Integration graph recorded for this wave, for the record.
review_asks.assessment: The wave's one system (c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9, 'Student Management System (VB.NET)') is recorded in systems[], with its two external touchpoints (a GitHub report link and the ACE OLEDB runtime) in external_deps[]. No cross-app data_flows[], shared_identifiers[], or cross_system_capabilities[] exist because the wave contains a single application with no peer to integrate with. The governing-profile mismatch Discovery flagged (this application has no detectable FAA/NAS relevance under the 'faa' governing profile) is carried forward in metadata.unresolved_references rather than silently adopted or restated as fact.

unresolved_references.finding: Governing-profile mismatch: the governing client profile for this task is declared as 'faa' (FAA/NAS legacy-modernization scope), but the sole application in this wave (c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9, 'Student Management System (VB.NET)') is a public, single-developer academic student-records desktop tool (GPL licence, public GitHub origin, one-commit history, author-credited project report) with no aviation, NAS, air-traffic, certification, or FAA-adjacent content of any kind. Both the Discovery catalog and structural-analysis passes independently raised this same discrepancy. This mapper does not adopt an alternative governing profile and does not restate one as fact here; it maps the application as found and flags the mismatch for the engagement owner to resolve before any FAA-specific gating (safety tiering, NAS impact assessment, compliance mapping) consumes this graph.

Single-application wave: the integration graph is cross-app by construction, so with only one application in scope there is no peer system to form a data_flows[] edge, a shared_identifiers[] entry, or a cross_system_capabilities[] cluster with. systems[] is populated for the one application present; data_flows[], shared_identifiers[], and cross_system_capabilities[] are left empty by design — a reflection of a genuine absence of integration partners, not an incomplete analysis.

No profiles/faa/risk-classification.yaml or profiles/faa/scoring.yaml was staged among this task's input artifacts, so no profile-driven tier/volume banding could be looked up for the system node. tier is intentionally left unset on the systems[] entry rather than guessed; the Discovery catalog's own safety_tier field is likewise null pending authoritative Safety Board input (it notes only a non-authoritative 'T3' lean from the FAA profile README's qualitative signal table).

Discovery's structural-analysis pass could not resolve Access column data types, nullability, primary-key/index definitions, or row counts for the application's sole table ('students') because the .accdb was decoded as a binary file and never opened through a live database engine; these remain open in discovery/c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9/structural-analysis.json's database-schema-summary.open_questions. Carried forward here as context for Rationalization; not independently re-verified by this mapper.

systems.name: Student Management System (VB.NET)
systems.description: Standalone Windows desktop (WinForms) application for managing student academic records (CRUD over a single 'students' table) with a statistics dashboard, persisted to a local Microsoft Access (.accdb) file. No HTTP, batch, or messaging surface. Single build project, single deployment surface — multi-subsystem decomposition thresholds (≥2 tech-stack families, ≥3 top-level subsystem directories, or a README naming ≥2 subsystems) are not met, so this is modeled as one system node rather than decomposed.
systems.deployment_surface: Student Management System.exe (single Windows desktop executable, x86, manually installed per workstation)

external_deps.name: GitHub-hosted project report (public PDF)
external_deps.owner: Unassigned — public GitHub repository under the original author's account; no internal/organizational owner recorded
external_deps.description: The dashboard's 'Report' button does not generate a report; it shells out via Process.Start to a hardcoded public github.com URL for the author's project-report PDF. The application's only outbound network call.

external_deps.name: Microsoft Access Database Engine (ACE OLEDB 12.0) redistributable
external_deps.owner: Microsoft (COTS runtime component); no internal owner recorded
external_deps.description: Out-of-process COM provider required on every workstation to open the bundled studentDB.accdb file; not a NuGet/assembly reference. Release build pins PlatformTarget x86, so the 32-bit redistributable specifically is required.
